feedback: If a learner uses fifteen and fifty interchangeably, contrast them directly: fifty = 5 tens; fifteen = 1 ten and 5 ones. Say them slowly, stressing -ty vs -teen, and pair each with its base-ten model.
If reading 76 drifts toward a teen word, re-anchor on the tens: seventy is 7 tens, then the ones word -six follows, giving seventy-six.
activities.intendedInsight: The '-ty' word names a number of tens (fifty = 5 tens) while the '-teen' word is a teen (fifteen = 1 ten and 5); linking each to a quantity removes the guesswork from the near-identical sounds.
learnerActions: Take a minimal pair such as fifteen/fifty and read both aloud, stressing the ending (-teen vs -ty).
Beside each word, write its numeral (fifteen = 15, fifty = 50) and show a matching quantity or base-ten model (fifteen = 1 ten and 5 ones; fifty = 5 tens).
Repeat with thirteen/thirty and other pairs, each time pairing word, numeral and quantity so meaning separates the near-identical sounds.
Answer a quick 'fifteen or fifty?' decision with the set of objects visible, choosing by quantity rather than guessing.
activities.title: Sound-alike contrast: '-teen' versus '-ty'

feedback: If the numeral comes out as 803 (or similarly 507 for fifty-seven), name the error (concatenating the spoken parts as full digits) and rebuild using a tens/ones frame so the ones digit sits in the ones place.
If teen and decade are swapped, return to the contrast pair with quantities before retrying.
Confirm success when the learner produces both directions correctly: 'seventy-six' for 76 and 83 for 'eighty-three'.
activities.intendedInsight: A learner who has the system can move fluently in both directions — word to numeral and numeral to word — without concatenating the spoken parts or confusing teen and decade words.
learnerActions: Given a label showing the numeral 76, write the words for a new label a customer could read ('seventy-six'), ordered correctly and hyphenated.
Given the word 'eighty-three' on a card, read it and write the numeral (83).
Check a friend's work: they wrote 803 for 'eighty-three' — decide whether it is right and explain what went wrong.
Compare 40 and 14 (and 'ninety' vs 'nineteen'): read each aloud and write each the other way to confirm you can move both directions.
activities.title: Use number words in a real read-and-write task
